issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency: The problem statement and template require an instance method named swiftExperienceDescription() on the Developer class and instruct calling it in the initializer, but the solution defines and calls a method named getExperienceDescription() instead. Problem statement: requests swiftExperienceDescription(); Template (Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift) declares func swiftExperienceDescription() -> String; Solution (Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift) implements func getExperienceDescription() -> String and calls print(self.getExperienceDescription()) in the initializer. This mismatch can cause automated checks that expect swiftExperienceDescription() to fail and will confuse students about which method name to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Rename the solution's getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription() and update the initializer call to print(self.swiftExperienceDescription()); or (B) Update the problem statement and template to require getExperienceDescription() and instruct calling getExperienceDescription() in the initializer. Ensure the method signature and the initializer call use the same identifier in all three places.

issues.description: The concept is a Developer instance method that returns a printable description of the developer's Swift experience. The problem statement and the provided template use the identifier swiftExperienceDescription() (problem_statement.md: line 35; template Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift: stub at line 24 and TODO to call it in the initializer at line 15). The solution instead defines and calls getExperienceDescription() (solution Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift: function declaration at line 24; call in initializer at line 15). Because the same conceptual behavior is given two different method names across artifacts, students comparing the template/problem to the reference solution may be confused about which method to implement and why the solution appears to use a different name, which creates unnecessary cognitive load and hinders straightforward mapping from requirement to implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier across artifacts. Either rename the solution's getExperienceDescription() function to swiftExperienceDescription() and update its call in the solution initializer to swiftExperienceDescription(), or update the problem statement and template to require getExperienceDescription() instead. Prefer renaming the solution to swiftExperienceDescription() to match the exercise instructions and the template stub so students can directly map the requirement to the reference implementation.
